moreHelp: You'll find more guides under the “How to use” tab.

overview.title: Overview
overview.intro: Your home screen shows how your pet is doing today and what's coming up, all in one place.

0.title: Read the colour status
0.body: Green means everything is fine. Orange warns that a due date is approaching — a booster shot or deworming, for example. Red means something is overdue and needs attention.

1.title: Take the next step
1.body: The “Next step” card always offers one concrete action — fill in missing data, do a check-in or record a vet visit. Just tap it.

2.title: Switch between pets
2.body: If you have several pets, the switcher in the header changes whose data you see. The overview recalculates instantly.

overview.tip: If the status seems strict, check the dates of your latest records in the Health Passport — the overview calculates due dates from them.

checkIn.title: Check-in
checkIn.intro: A quick weekly note on how your pet is doing. In a few seconds you build up a history that reveals patterns later.

0.title: Answer one question
0.body: Choose whether everything is fine, you noticed a change, or you're not sure. That alone is enough — you can save the check-in right away.

1.title: Add details if you want
1.body: Under “Add details” you can record weight, appetite, energy, stool, skin and coat, and behaviour changes. The more you fill in, the sharper the later insights.

2.title: Watch the trend
2.body: Below the form you'll find the history and trend. If the same symptom keeps coming back, Pawly flags it and offers to open a health episode.

checkIn.tip: Consistency matters most. Even a weekly “all fine” is a valuable record — without it there's no way to tell what normal looks like for your pet.

food.title: Food
food.intro: A record of what your pet currently eats — including treats and supplements. Pawly then links it to your check-ins.

0.title: Set the current food
0.body: Enter the product name and the date your pet started eating it. The previous food is closed automatically and moved to history.

1.title: Add treats and supplements
1.body: Keep a separate list of everything your pet gets besides the main food. Treats are a common hidden source of allergens.

2.title: Look at the insights
2.body: The insights card compares food changes with symptoms from your check-ins — for example, whether digestive trouble started only after switching to a new food.

food.tip: To find out whether a food suits your pet's allergies, send its ingredient list to Analysis — the result feeds back here.

analyze.title: Food analysis
analyze.intro: Enter a food's ingredient list and AI evaluates it against your pet's profile, allergens included.

0.title: Enter the ingredients
0.body: Either type the ingredient list from the packaging, or simply photograph or upload the label and Pawly will read the text for you.

1.title: Check which pet you're analysing for
1.body: The analysis runs against the selected pet's profile. The allergies and health conditions stored there decide what the app warns you about.

2.title: Read the result
2.body: You get a score, a breakdown of pros and cons, and highlighted risky ingredients. The result is saved to History automatically so you can come back to it.

analyze.tip: Photo quality decides the outcome. Shoot the ingredient list close up, straight on and in good light — blurry text is harder for the AI to read.

profiles.title: Pet profiles
profiles.intro: The foundation of the whole app. Food analysis, the health passport and the vet card all draw on the profile.

0.title: Fill in the basics
0.body: Name, species, breed, date of birth and weight. Age and breed let Pawly judge its recommendations better.

1.title: Add allergies and health conditions
1.body: This is the most important part. Every allergy or intolerance you record turns into a warning during food analysis.

2.title: Add more pets
2.body: You can keep several profiles. Switch between pets in the header — each one has its own passport, diary and history.

profiles.tip: A profile isn't a one-off. When something new turns up — a new allergy, a chronic condition — come back and add it.

passport.title: Health passport
passport.intro: A digital replacement for the paper booklet. Vaccinations, dewormings, parasite treatments, medication, visits and weight in one place.

0.title: Import your old booklet
0.body: Got a paper record? Photograph it via AI import and Pawly will extract the individual entries. It shows them for review before saving — always go through them.

1.title: Add records as you go
1.body: Use “New record” to log a vaccination, deworming, visit or medication. For a vet visit you can add everything that happened during it at once.

2.title: Keep track of due dates
2.body: Records with a next-dose date show up automatically in the Overview and in Reminders, so booster shots take care of themselves.

passport.tip: AI import handles multiple pages at once. Photograph the whole booklet page by page and upload them together to save yourself the typing.

addRecord.title: New record
addRecord.intro: The form for logging what happened — from a single vaccination to a whole vet visit with medication and expenses.

0.title: Choose what you're recording
0.body: You can pick a quick single-item entry, the manual form, or AI import from a photo of the paper booklet. Use AI import for old history and the manual form for today's visit.

1.title: Fill in the visit basics
1.body: Date, clinic and reason. This is the backbone of the record — everything else hangs off it.

2.title: Attach what happened during the visit
2.body: In the linked records section you enable a vaccination, deworming, parasite treatment, therapy, medication or food change. They are saved together with expenses and notes, so the visit stays in one piece.

addRecord.tip: You don't have to fill in everything. A date and a record type are enough — you can add the rest later from the record detail.

diary.title: Health diary
diary.intro: A place for health episodes — vomiting, limping, skin problems, behaviour changes. It exists so that next time you know what worked.

0.title: Record what happened
0.body: Date, category and a short description. You can attach a photo too — a rash, for instance, looks different a week later.

1.title: Write down what helped
1.body: This is the part people most often skip and the one with the most value. Record the treatment and whether it worked.

2.title: Use the similar-episode summary
2.body: For each new episode the AI pulls together a summary of similar past records, so you can immediately see whether it's a recurring problem and how it was handled.

diary.tip: The filters above the list help you find every episode in one category — all digestive problems over the past year, for example.

vetCard.title: Vet card
vetCard.intro: A one-page summary you can print or show on your phone during a vet visit.

0.title: Check the contents
0.body: The card draws on the profile, health passport and diary. Go through it and confirm the data is current — especially active medication.

1.title: Print it or save as PDF
1.body: The print button prepares a version without on-screen controls. In the print dialog you can choose to save as PDF and send it by e-mail.

2.title: Take it to the appointment
2.body: Your vet immediately sees the vaccination history, chronic conditions and recent problems without you having to remember everything.

vetCard.tip: Prepare the card before you leave home. There's rarely enough time at the clinic and it's easy to forget something important.

history.title: Analysis history
history.intro: An archive of every food analysis you've run.

0.title: Find an older analysis
0.body: Records are sorted newest first. Open any of them to get the full result along with the reasoning.

1.title: Compare foods
1.body: When choosing between two products, open both analyses and compare the scores and the lists of risky ingredients.

2.title: Set the winner as current food
2.body: Once you decide, record the food on the Food page — from then on it links up with your check-ins.

history.tip: History is tied to your account, not your device. Sign in on another phone and you'll find it exactly as you left it.

notifications.title: Reminders
notifications.intro: Choose what Pawly should e-mail you about, and how far in advance.

0.title: Turn on e-mail reminders
0.body: The main switch controls whether you get e-mails at all. Without it, due dates are still calculated and visible in the Overview — you just won't be notified.

1.title: Pick the record types
1.body: Enable vaccinations, dewormings, parasite treatments, check-ups and medication separately. Simply switch off whatever you don't need.

2.title: Set the lead time
2.body: Choose how many days ahead you want to be warned. You can pick several values at once — 30 days and 7 days before a vaccination, for example.

notifications.tip: Reminders are based on the dates in your Health Passport. If nothing arrives, check that your records have a next-dose date filled in.

settings.title: Settings
settings.intro: App appearance, language and account management, including your data.

0.title: Choose appearance and language
0.body: The light and dark mode switch and the language selector. The setting stays on this device.

1.title: Export your data
1.body: You can download everything we hold about your pets at any time, in a machine-readable format.

2.title: Tidy up your account
2.body: This is also where you sign out or permanently delete your account. Deleting is irreversible and removes all health records too.

settings.tip: Export your data before deleting the account. Once confirmed, it cannot be recovered.
